title: On Relativity Theory and Openness of the Future
relevance: Constructs a relativistically appropriate notion of becoming/open future and rebuts inference from absence of global present to determinism.
section_locator: Opening abstract and pp. 147-167; especially p.159 text on absence of analogue to Einstein distant simultaneity in GR.
assumptions: Special relativistic causal structure; event-relative causal past/future rather than global simultaneity; probabilistic indeterminacy is not defined by a universal present slice.
conclusion: SR does not by itself exclude all indeterminateness/becoming; global present is not required for event-relative becoming.
proof_status: Philosophical/physical argument, not a formal theorem audited here.
open_questions: How exactly are local becoming relations generalized in curved spacetimes and stochastic dynamics?
limits: Philosophical argument; no formal theorem audit.
bib_audit_note: Bibliography verified via Crossref 10.1086/289609 (Philosophy of Science 58(2):147-167, 1991). Replaced third-party aggregator (paperzz.com) URL with the canonical DOI; aggregator copy not re-inspected in this audit. [kb-bib-repair 2026-10-19 audit]

title: Discussion: On Relativity Theory and Openness of the Future

proof_status: Philosophical argument; no independent reconstruction beyond accessed text.
open_questions: Can a precise stochastic model adjudicate whether the disagreement is empirical or interpretive?

title: Time and Physical Geometry
version: The Journal of Philosophy 64(8), 1967, pp.240-247; JSTOR DOI 10.2307/2024493
relevance: Influential Rietdijk-Putnam route from special relativity to block-universe/eternalism and critique of objective becoming.
section_locator: pp.240-242, scanned full text encountered via author paper copy indexed at https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Gary-Stephens-3/post/Apropos_the_Andromeda_paradox_How_exactly_are_the_observers_moving_and_how_are_the_events_at_the_distant_galaxy_so_arranged/attachment/62b33de3935b37798d074ee7/AS%3A1169797052141570%401655912759328/download/putnam_1967.pdf
assumptions: Relativity of simultaneity plus an interpretation of simultaneity/reality and transitivity of equality in existential status across overlapping observer presents.
conclusion: Putnam argues that past/present/future ontological asymmetry is untenable, then adopts a block view; physics alone supplies kinematic structure, while bridge claims carry ontology.
proof_status: Partial text only, not a complete argument audit; treatment of transitivity and modal alternatives remains contested.
open_questions: Which premise connects coordinate simultaneity to equal existence status, and can local becoming avoid it?

assumptions: Minkowski spacetime, causal connectibility, inertial observer worldline, candidate simultaneity definability and stated invariance/relational conditions.
conclusion: They argue removing temporal-reflection invariance admits null-cone alternatives; Einstein synchrony remains unique if the relevant convention must be observer-position independent within a frame.
proof_status: Authors' mathematical constructions read from primary source; not independently reproduced.
open_questions: Does the full Malament proof formulation or later analysis answer the physical status of temporal-reflection invariance?
limits: Primary criticism, not a substitute for primary Malament text; no proof reproduction.
